name: Nethanel
overview: Nethanel was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically as the scribe and the father of Shemaiah. His role as a scribe indicates a position of responsibility in preserving and managing sacred writings or records within the Levitical community. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethanel means 'G-d [El] has given,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in divine provision. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 24:6, underscoring its biblical origin and usage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Nethanel as the father of Shemaiah, as inferred from 1 Chronicles 24:6. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Nethanel's significance in the biblical narrative arises from his Levitical heritage and his role as a scribe, which would have been vital for maintaining the purity and accuracy of the sacred texts and genealogies. Being the father of Shemaiah connects him to the continuation of Levitical duties and responsibilities, highlighting the importance of faithful service within the tribe of Levi. His mention in 1 Chronicles underscores the value placed on lineage and the transmission of religious roles in Israel's history.
